comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Credit Quality Deterioration and Economic Uncertainty
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the net charge-off ratio increased driven by credit card loans and commercial real estate office portfolios. Commercial reservable criticized exposure and nonperforming loans also increased. Uncertainty remains regarding broader economic impacts from inflation, elevated rates, and geopolitical issues, which could adversely impact future credit quality.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America reported an increase in net credit losses/charge-offs for 2024, attributing the rise to the maturation or seasoning of recent credit card vintages and macroeconomic pressures such as inflation and interest rates. Citi specifically noted that lower FICO band customers drove the increase, while BAC highlighted credit card loans as a primary driver alongside commercial real estate, and cited uncertainty regarding broader economic impacts from inflationary pressures and elevated rates.

sentences.text: As presented in the chart above, the fourth quarter of 2024 net credit loss rate in Branded Cards was broadly stable quarter-over-quarter.
The net credit loss rate increased year-over-year, primarily reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years.
In addition, the increase was driven by macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment, with lower FICO band customers primarily driving the increase.
During 2024, our net charge-off ratio increased primarily driven by credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio.

Uncertainty remains regarding broader economic impacts due to higher costs associated with inflationary pressures experienced over the past several years, elevated rates as well as the current geopolitical environment, and could lead to adverse impacts to credit quality metrics in future periods.

comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Credit Portfolio Credit Losses and Reserves
comparisons.peer_summary: Net charge-offs for the consumer portfolio increased by $1.1 billion to $4.2 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher credit card loan charge-offs, while the allowance for loan and lease losses remained relatively unchanged at $8.6 billion compared to 2023. The macroeconomic environment during 2024 featured stable U.S. unemployment rates and steadily increasing home prices.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and Bank of America both disclosed year-over-year increases in net credit losses/charge-offs for consumer credit products in 2024, driven by the aging of recent loan vintages and higher credit card charge-offs. Citi described the Q4 rate as stable quarter-over-quarter but up year-over-year due to vintage maturation, while BAC reported a $1.1 billion increase in consumer net charge-offs primarily due to higher credit card loan charge-offs, supported by a macroeconomic environment of stable unemployment but elevated inflation and rates.

sentences.text: The net credit loss rate increased year-over-year, primarily reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years.
The maturation was delayed by unprecedented levels of government stimulus during the pandemic.
In addition, the increase was driven by macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment, with lower FICO band customers primarily driving the increase.
During 2024, the U.S. unemployment rate remained relatively stable, and home prices increased steadily throughout most of 2024.
Net charge-offs increased $1.1 billion to $4.2 billion in 2024 primarily due to higher credit card loan charge-offs.
